params.body:
The statement and the register were written against Proof-of-Control draft v0.1: claims keyed to its chapters and rows (C4, 4.1.1, 8.1.5), each with a tier written by hand. The standard is now a Working Draft v1.0 with six named domains, no row ids, and a stricter tier rule. Every row the statement cites is gone from that text, and nothing let a reader recompute a tier.

This splits the mapping in two, so the system's description stops depending on one draft's numbering.

- `conformance/facts.json`: 13 facts under ids this repo owns (the 8 rows of the statement, plus `policy-versioned`, `revocable`, `far-end-verified`, `halts-on-mismatch` and the designed `bounded-by-working-set`). Each names its mechanism, its evidence paths, its status, and the parties it asks a reader to trust, typed by kind (hardware-vendor-attestation, timestamp-authority, operator-service-key, ...).
- `conformance/standards/aais-poc-0.1.json` and `aais-poc-1.0-draft.json`: for each version, where every fact lands and how far each kind of party lets a fact rise, with the standard's words as the reason. A cap the text does not settle is marked as a reading.
- `cmd/conformance`: computes the tier as the lowest cap among a fact's parties (a set of independent parties counts as one only where the standard allows it), compares two versions (`--against`), and shows the effect of proposed rules (`--assume-proposed`).
- `docs/conformance-model.md`: the model on one page.

The tests hold that every evidence path exists, that every standard grades every kind of party the facts use, and that graded against v0.1 the facts give back exactly the tiers `register.json` declares. Nothing in the statement or the register changes here.

What it shows against the v1.0 draft (read 9 October 2026, open for comment until 30 October):

- `history-anchored` and `agent-identified` drop from Tier 3 to Tier 2: the draft names a certificate authority and a permissioned or consortium chain as single trusted parties. `admitted-on-token` drops on a reading of the domain.
- No fact clears Tier 3, so under that draft nothing here is Proof-of-Control.
- With the proposal to accept a threshold of independent parties (comment [ai] on Section 6), `history-anchored` returns to Tier 3.
- Intel's attestation and Google's platform hold most facts at Tier 2.

Two inconsistencies the model surfaced, left for a separate change:

- The README says two Tier 4 rows hold through the halt on a mismatch; the halt also rests on Intel and Google, so the model grades it Tier 2.
- The README says `#portal` is a key in the environment of an ordinary server; it has been in Cloud KMS since 11 September 2026.

`go test ./...` passes.
params.title: Conformance as facts and crosswalks, tiers computed per standard version
